issue_context.title: Support Equity Quotes
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
Lean should be able to process Equity quotes. 

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
Lean can only backtest equity with trades.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
Modifications in code:
- Add `QuoteBars` for equities in `DefaultDataTypes`
https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/b84263840b2d149604463c3d61d98bff7e697f36/Common/Data/SubscriptionManager.cs#L207

- If `QuoteBar` will be the default tick type for Equity, we should modify `GetCommonTickType`
https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/b84263840b2d149604463c3d61d98bff7e697f36/Common/Util/LeanData.cs#L620

- Here only one subscription is added for equities, we need to add two subscriptions.
https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/b84263840b2d149604463c3d61d98bff7e697f36/Algorithm/QCAlgorithm.Universe.cs#L454

Those modifications were included in [this branch](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/tree/equity-taq-wip). It shows an expected behavior using a basic `QCAlogorithm` and a Framework algorithm. But it is a simple draft, new tests should be added, the regressions test expected values need to update. Also, we need to include new sample data.

review_comments:
Some more ideas for testing:
- Could also add an assert for the subscriptions in the `OnSecurityChanges` callback, make sure expected types are added correctly
- Could check that the data is actually being pumped into the algorithm at `OnData`
- Could make a 1 time history request during initialize and check the correct data is sent there too
Why is this `_canTrade` flag required? Wondering the same for the `DataNormalizationMode.Raw` ?

> Why is this _canTrade flag required?

The algorithm trades each 15 minutes, but if it sends an order at 16:00 it'll be an open market order an it fill price won't be the quote side **close**, but the the quote side **open**.

So to keep it simple, I don't allow it to send orders after 15:45.

`DataNormalizationMode.Raw` is just because it was easier to check prices directly from the file data :slightly_smiling_face:
This will test market orders, think we should test other order types too (maybe unit test)? Thinking about which price should the fill models use 🤔
